answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by pricing identity: every agent locks a non-transferable stake that is burned when its reports prove false. Spinning up a thousand fakes means locking a thousand stakes, and each clone stays individually liable, so one dishonest claim forfeits that agent's stake. Attestations must be countersigned by peers with their own stake at risk, so a rogue agent that tries to wander into a compliant set finds no backer. With no cheap meadow of free identities, an attacker's plume of fake reputation collapses, and flooding the network costs more than it pays.
